name: Feeless instant pay-per-call
text: Current pay-per-call for AI agents (x402/USDC) routes every call through a trusted verifier that checks the stablecoin payment and releases the HTTP 402; tiny charges get batched because fees make micro-calls uneconomic.

name: On-chain payment verification
text: The service must confirm a payment before serving; existing solutions trust an interposed verifier or an API key shared out of band instead of the chain itself.

name: Agent self-custody wallet SDK
text: An agent holds its own Nano keys (seed-derived address) and transacts via rpc.nano.to; today SDKs are library-specific and require knowing Nano crypto (blake2b hashing, ed25519 signing, proof-of-work).

name: Service-side price and credit tools
text: A service that sells per-call API access needs to set a price, see incoming falls, credit/cancel; current MCP pay servers put the settlement layer outside the server.

name: Program-reproducible payment flow
text: End-to-end pay-per-call must be reproducible by a script/agent with no human step; current flows assume a wallet GUI or a manual approval.

name: No-node instant usability
text: Nano's weakness is that transacting needs signing + proof-of-work and usually a synced node; the fix should let any agent hold and pay from a single HTTP RPC endpoint.

name: Borrow a mechanism from another field
text: Design a per-call payment scheme by combining Nano settlement with a mechanism from another field (e.g. control theory, ledgers, token buckets).

name: MCP-native payment ergonomics
text: The pay-per-call flow should feel native inside a Model Context Protocol server: an agent calls a tool, pays in Nano, gets the answer.

name: Replay and idempotency safety
text: Per-call payments must not be double-spent by retries or replayed proofs; each call is paid exactly once.

name: Proof-of-payment grant + on-chain settle
text: Grant access fast on proof, then settle on-chain, so the agent is not blocked on finality.
